answer: A port wharf charges every ship a docking bond before it can trade, and an agent economy can do the same: each identity must lock a refundable stake that is slashed on proven fraud. A Sybil attacker must then pay for every fake identity, so the cost of the attack scales linearly instead of being free. Like water seeping through karst, cheap identities keep leaking in, but a bond turns each one from free into expensive, while honest agents earn their stake back from a shared lagoon of reputation built over time.
